Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Acme Health's use cases and compliance bar. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

What we covered
- SOC 2: Redwood Inference completed Type II testing for 2025; SOC 2 report is available (we usually provide a redacted PDF). Full SOC 2/attestation timeline: annual reports, + bridge letter if needed.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We support GDPR controls; for HIPAA we offer a BAA and our Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem) for PHI-sensitive flows.
- Vendor security questionnaire: you mentioned a standard security questionnaire — please send it and we'll start filling it out.
- Telemetry / cookies: You asked what telemetry is collected by the Console and on our public docs site (analytics/cookies) — see questions below.

Immediate next steps
1) Can you send the vendor security questionnaire (or upload to the shared Drive link)?
2) We will share our redacted SOC 2 report + bridge letter (attached).
3) I'll loop in Rishi (security) and Monica (CS) to draft answers and schedule a security review call.

Telemetry / privacy clarifications (so we have the right info for your questionnaire)
- Console telemetry: aggregated usage metrics, request latency, error rates. By default we do not store raw user-uploaded PHI in telemetry; request logs may contain hashed identifiers and truncated IPs for troubleshooting.
- Docs site: we use third-party analytics (Google Analytics) and standard cookies for site usage tracking. No console-level auth or API keys are exposed on the docs site.

Attachments included: RID-SOC2-2025-bridge-letter.pdf (redacted) and SOC2-report-2025-redacted.pdf

Happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up with your security team next week — what windows work for you?

Thanks,

Marissa / Monica —

Thanks for the ping. Quick answers and next steps (I attached a draft of prelim-acme-answers.xlsx with cell-level comments):

Telemetry / logs
- Console telemetry: we collect aggregated usage metrics (counts, latencies, error rates). We do not store raw user-submitted content in telemetry.
- Identifiers: we do not store unhashed email addresses in telemetry by default. Some operational logs may contain hashed or truncated identifiers for debugging; these are stored with access controls and retention policies.
- IPs: we truncate IPs to /24 for retention and troubleshooting; full IPs are available only for 7 days in raw logs for incident response.

Docs site / cookies
- We use Google Analytics (GA4) and a first-party cookie for session. We do not run Hotjar on the docs site. GA4 may collect client identifiers; GA settings are configured to disable user-level cross-site tracking where possible.

HIPAA / BAA
- Redwood is willing to sign a BAA for PHI processing. For PHI-sensitive flows we recommend Private (VPC) deployment to minimize surface area; Hosted can be used with strong data-minimization and encryption in transit but may require additional controls and contractual terms. We will prepare a short recommendation matrix for Monica to include in the customer reply.

Next steps
1) I'll populate the security sections in the questionnaire (see attached).
2) Propose security call Tue 2026-06-23 10:00 AM PT — I'll invite our security SME.
3) We'll upload the draft answers to the Drive link and send to Liam for review by EOD Tue.
